answer: Sybil resistance here ties identity to bonded stake plus a proof-of-work kernel each new agent must compute on registration, making mass fake accounts costly in compute and capital. Every epoch, a random challenge samples agents; honest ones earn copper credits that raise their weight, while duplicate identities fail the check. A rising tide of verified peers dilutes adversaries' influence only if they pay the same bond, so creating N sybils costs N times stake plus work, capping the payoff.
